# Action reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate-action-reference.mjs in the cellucid repository from the action
     catalogue (assets/js/app/actions/definitions/). Do not edit: run that script.
     tests/action-reference-contract.test.mjs fails while this page differs from what it writes. -->

This page answers: **"What can be done to an open dataset, by name, and what does each step
change?"** Every change a person makes with a control, and every change or read an agent,
a Python or R viewer, a session or a replay makes, is one of these actions, checked
against the same parameters and recorded as one history step with the same label. The
catalogue is `assets/js/app/actions/definitions/` in the `cellucid` repository
(`app/actions/README.md` there); this page is generated from it. How the action layer, the
state domains and the history work is {doc}`29_action_layer_domains_and_history`.

The catalogue holds 177 actions: 96 that change the state or open a dataset, 37 that move or edit the history, 13 that act outside the state (a file written, a publication, what this browser keeps), and 31 reads.
Parameters name things, never positions: a field as `{source, key}` (`obs` for a column of
the cells, `var` for a gene), a category by its label, a gene by its name, a highlight page
by its name, a view as `"live"` or `"View N"`, and cells by their original position (the
0-based row of `obs`). A step therefore replays on another dataset with the same names. An
agent calls an action by its tool name (the type with dots and dashes as underscores).

## State domains

An action names the parts of the state it changes ("Changes"). The history keeps their values
before and after each step; undo puts the before-values back. It also names the parts its
result depends on besides its parameters ("Depends on": the cells, mapping or pages it computes
from, the state a name it is given resolves in); a step keeps their value hashes, which say
when its result is stale.

| Domain | Name | Holds |
|---|---|---|
| `cells` | Open cells | Which cells are open (every cell, or a subsample) and how many of them genes are read for. |
| `mapping` | Data mapping | Which stored arrays are plotted and read (the data mapping). |
| `field-overlays` | Fields and labels | Field and category renames, deleted fields, user-defined fields with their values. |
| `gene-sets` | Gene sets | Gene sets pushed by a notebook or made in the app. |
| `views` | Views | Kept views, their layout, the focused view, camera lock, the representation each view shows. |
| `active-field` | Active field | What each view is coloured by (a field or a gene). |
| `filters` | Filters | Category visibility, continuous ranges, outlier and missing-value filters, per view. |
| `colors` | Colors | Category colours, colour maps, colour ranges, log scale, zero grey, per view. |
| `visibility` | Hidden cells | Cells hidden one by one (the cell visibility mask), per view. |
| `highlights` | Highlights | Highlight pages and their groups of cells. |
| `camera` | Camera | The camera of each view and the navigation mode. |
| `camera-path` | Camera path | Camera path keyframes and their playback settings. |
| `settings` | Settings | Render, navigation and overlay settings (every stable control of the sidebar). |
| `analysis` | Analysis | The analyses of the panel and of each window: their settings and results. |
| `layout` | Layout | Docked and floating panels, analysis windows' places and sizes, open sections, sidebar, theme. |

## History

### `history.anndata.save`

**Save AnnData with this state.** Write a new Cellucid-ready AnnData file (.zarr.zip) of the whole open dataset with the state shown applied, as Python and R apply a session: renamed labels, user-defined fields and highlight groups as obs columns, gene sets in uns and var, and a record of what was applied; never over the dataset's own file.

- Agent tool: `history_anndata_save`
- Effect: `outside`: it acts outside the dataset's state and history (writes a file the person receives, publishes, or keeps or removes something in this browser for later visits), which the history cannot take back, and records no step
- Asks the person first when an agent takes it: it writes a file (`writes-file`)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `file` | string | no | The new file's name (.zarr.zip is added when it does not end so); "&lt;dataset> with this state.zarr.zip" when left out. Not empty. |

Example:

```json
{}
```

It returns:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `file` | string | The file's name. |
| `to` | one of `"file"`, `"download"` | file: a file the person chose in the save dialog; download: the browser's downloads. |
| `bytes` | integer |  |
| `layout` | one of `"anndata"`, `"mudata"` | A Cellucid-ready AnnData, or a MuData for a dataset of several modalities. |
| `cells` | integer | Cells written: every cell of the dataset, whichever were open. |
| `tracker` | object (`id`, `name`) |  |
| `branch` | object (`id`, `name`) |  |
| `step` | string | The step applied: the one shown. |
| `applied` | boolean | False when every change was in the dataset already (no record added). |
| `rows` | list of object (`kind`, `name`, `status`, `cells`, `note`) | Every change of the apply plan, in domain order, as Python and R plan it. |
| `left_out` | list of string | What the copy does not hold of the state, or of the dataset, one sentence each. |

Timeline label: Saved an AnnData copy with this state

Pseudocode: `save_anndata()`

### `history.bookmark.set`

**Bookmark a step.** Give a step a bookmark name, unique in its tracker (jump to it by name), or remove it with null. Bookmark before destructive or heavy work.

- Agent tool: `history_bookmark_set`
- Effect: `history`: it moves or edits the history itself and records no step of the state (an edit is kept in the history's journal, undone from Recently deleted)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `step` | string | yes | A step of the tracker in use, by its id (history_get lists the steps). |
| `name` | string or null | yes | The bookmark, or null to remove it. Not empty. |

Example:

```json
{"step":"s3","name":"Before reclustering"}
```

It returns:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `step` | string |  |
| `bookmark` | string or null |  |
| `journal` | string |  |

Timeline label: Bookmarked step s3 "Before reclustering"

Pseudocode: `bookmark("s3", "Before reclustering")`

### `history.branch.apply`

**Apply a branch's steps here.** Apply a branch's own steps again, by name, on top of the step shown, as a new branch (no values are merged; a step that does not apply here is flagged).

- Agent tool: `history_branch_apply`
- Effect: `history`: it moves or edits the history itself and records no step of the state (an edit is kept in the history's journal, undone from Recently deleted)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `branch` | string | yes | A branch by its name or its id (history_summary lists them). Not empty. |
| `name` | string | no | A name, unique among its kind (compared without case and extra spaces); no length limit. Not empty. |
| `tracker` | string | no | A tracker by its name or its id (history_summary lists them); the tracker in use when left out. Not empty. |

Example:

```json
{"branch":"Main"}
```

It returns:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `branch` | object (`id`, `name`) or null |  |
| `head` | string | The step shown now. |
| `report` | list of object (`source`, `label`, `outcome`, `step`, `reason`, `missing`) | Every step replayed and what became of it. |

Timeline label: Applied the steps of branch "Main" here

Pseudocode: `apply_branch(branch="Main")`

### `history.branch.delete`

**Delete a branch.** Move a branch's own steps (those no other branch starts from) to Recently deleted, where they can be restored; with with_sub_branches, the branches that start from it too. Main and locked branches cannot be deleted.

- Agent tool: `history_branch_delete`
- Effect: `history`: it moves or edits the history itself and records no step of the state (an edit is kept in the history's journal, undone from Recently deleted)
- Asks the person first when an agent takes it: it deletes something saved (`deletes-saved`)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `branch` | string | yes | A branch by its name or its id (history_summary lists them). Not empty. |
| `with_sub_branches` | boolean | no | Also delete every branch that starts from it. Default `false`. |
| `tracker` | string | no | A tracker by its name or its id (history_summary lists them); the tracker in use when left out. Not empty. |

Example:

```json
{"branch":"Main"}
```

It returns:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `branches` | list of object (`id`, `name`) | The branches deleted. |
| `steps` | integer | Steps moved to Recently deleted. |
| `results` | integer | Results computed on them. |
| `kept_views` | integer | Kept views elsewhere made from it (they keep their picture). |
| `replays` | integer | Trackers replayed from it. |
| `absorbed_by` | object (`id`, `name`) or null | The branch that keeps its shared steps. |
| `head` | string | The step shown now. |
| `journal` | string | Its Recently deleted entry. |

Timeline label: Deleted branch "Main"

Pseudocode: `delete_branch(branch="Main")`

### `history.clear`

**Clear the history.** Start the branch "Fresh start" from the opening step with nothing behind it: keeping the state shown (one squashed step from the dataset as opened to it), or from the dataset as opened (the branch starts with the next change). Every branch stays, archivable; either way it is kept in Recently changed and can be undone there.

- Agent tool: `history_clear`
- Effect: `history`: it moves or edits the history itself and records no step of the state (an edit is kept in the history's journal, undone from Recently deleted)
- Asks the person first when an agent takes it: it deletes something saved (`deletes-saved`)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `keep_state` | boolean | yes | True keeps the state shown as one step; false starts over from the dataset as opened. |

Example:

```json
{"keep_state":true}
```

It returns:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `branch` | object (`id`, `name`) or null |  |
| `head` | string | The step shown now. |
| `journal` | string | Its Recently changed entry. |

Timeline label: Cleared the history, keeping the state

Pseudocode: `clear_history(keep_state=True)`

### `history.diff`

**Compare two steps.** What differs between the state after two steps, part by part (filters, labels, highlights, …); the steps may be of two trackers.

- Agent tool: `history_diff`
- Effect: `read`: it reads, changes nothing and records no step

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `a` | object (`step`, `tracker`) | yes | The first step. |
| `b` | object (`step`, `tracker`) | yes | The second step. |

Example:

```json
{"a":{"step":"s1"},"b":{"step":"s2"}}
```

It returns:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `a` | object (`tracker`, `step`) |  |
| `b` | object (`tracker`, `step`) |  |
| `common` | string or null | Their last common step (null across trackers). |
| `domains` | list of object (`domain`, `name`, `lines`) |  |

### `history.get`

**Read the history.** The steps taken on this dataset, who took each (person, agent, notebook), branches and the step shown.

- Agent tool: `history_get`
- Effect: `read`: it reads, changes nothing and records no step

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tracker` | string | no | A tracker by its name or its id (history_summary lists them); the tracker in use when left out. Not empty. |
| `branch` | string | no | The path to this branch's tip (by its name or id) instead of the path to the step shown; not with all_branches. Not empty. |
| `all_branches` | boolean | no | Every branch, not only the path to the step shown. Default `false`. |
| `since` | number | no | Only the steps recorded at or after this time (milliseconds since 1970: a step's "at"), so a second read lists what came since. |
| `limit` | integer | no | The steps of one page (200 when left out: well under what a tool result carries). At least 1. Default `200`. |
| `cursor` | string | no | Where the page starts: the next of the last page (its last step's id); the first page when left out. Not empty. |
| `fields` | list of one of `"params"`, `"notes"`, `"bookmark"` | no | What to add to each step: params (each parameter in words), notes, bookmark. Each once. |

Example:

```json
{}
```

It returns:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `tracker` | object (`id`, `name`) |  |
| `trackers` | list of object (`id`, `name`, `active`) |  |
| `head` | string | The step shown now. |
| `branches` | list of object (`name`, `tip`, `active`) |  |
| `steps` | list of object (`id`, `parent`, `kind`, `squash`, `label`, `type`, `v`, `code`, `origin`, `agent`, `host`, `turn`, `at`, `status`, `note`, `touches`, `group`, `shown`, `params`, `notes`, `bookmark`) | One page: root first; parents before children. |
| `total` | integer | Steps on every page (the path to the step shown, or every branch). |
| `next` | string or null | The cursor of the next page; null on the last. |

### `history.journal.undo`

**Restore from Recently deleted.** Undo an edit of the history (a delete, a rename, a note, …) from Recently deleted: exactly as it was when nothing changed it since, else as new objects ("X (restored)", removed steps applied again as a branch). Undoing a rename whose old name was taken since is refused, naming the name to use instead.

- Agent tool: `history_journal_undo`
- Effect: `history`: it moves or edits the history itself and records no step of the state (an edit is kept in the history's journal, undone from Recently deleted)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `entry` | string | yes | An entry of Recently deleted, by its id (history_summary counts them). |
| `tracker` | string | no | A tracker by its name or its id (history_summary lists them); the tracker in use when left out. Not empty. |

Example:

```json
{"entry":"j0"}
```

It returns:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `entry` | string |  |
| `restored` | one of `"exact"`, `"as-new"` |  |
| `journal` | string | The entry the restore itself made (undoable). |
| `branch` | object (`id`, `name`) or null | The first branch a restore as new made of the steps it applied again. |
| `report` | list of object (`source`, `label`, `outcome`, `step`, `reason`, `missing`) | The steps a restore as new applied again and what became of each (empty for an exact restore). |

| `groups` | list of object (`id`, `name`, `branch`, `first`, `last`, `steps`, `notes`) | Every group, in id order: a named run of consecutive steps of one branch. |
| `bookmarks` | list of object (`name`, `step`) |  |
| `turns` | list of object (`id`, `label`, `by`, `steps`, `branch`, `summary`) |  |
| `stale` | integer | Results whose inputs changed since (history_stale lists them). |
| `recently_deleted` | integer | Entries that can be undone. |

### `history.tour.start`

**Start the guided tour.** Play the State panel's guided tour of the branch shown, from the opening to the step shown: each step is shown in turn with its caption and notes (a camera step is flown to), for a talk or a class. It returns once the tour plays; the person pauses, steps or stops it, or history_tour_stop does.

- Agent tool: `history_tour_start`
- Effect: `history`: it moves or edits the history itself and records no step of the state (an edit is kept in the history's journal, undone from Recently deleted)

It takes no parameters.

Example:

```json
{}
```

It returns:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `tracker` | object (`id`, `name`) |  |
| `branch` | object (`id`, `name`) |  |
| `steps` | integer | Steps the tour shows after the opening. |
| `returns_to` | string | The step shown again when the tour ends. |

Timeline label: Started the guided tour

Pseudocode: `tour_start()`

### `history.tour.stop`

**Stop the guided tour.** Stop the guided tour, as its Stop button does: the history returns to the step shown before it began (unless the person made a step meanwhile).

- Agent tool: `history_tour_stop`
- Effect: `history`: it moves or edits the history itself and records no step of the state (an edit is kept in the history's journal, undone from Recently deleted)

It takes no parameters.

Example:

```json
{}
```

It returns:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `stopped` | boolean | False when no tour was playing. |
| `head` | string or null | The step shown now. |

Timeline label: Stopped the guided tour

Pseudocode: `tour_stop()`

### `history.tracker.remove`

**Remove a tracker.** Move a tracker to Recently deleted, where it can be restored; when it is the one in use, the one used before it is shown first.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tracker` | string | yes | A tracker by its name or its id (history_summary lists them). Not empty. |

```json
{"tracker":"Tracker 1"}
```

It returns:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `tracker` | object (`id`, `name`) |  |
| `shown` | object (`id`, `name`) |  |
| `journal` | string |  |

Timeline label: Removed the tracker "Tracker 1"

Pseudocode: `remove_tracker("Tracker 1")`

## Fields

### `category.delete`

**Delete a category.** Move every cell of one category into the unassigned category. A column from the file becomes a new column (the original moves to Deleted fields); a column made in the app is edited in place.

- Agent tool: `category_delete`
- Effect: `state`: it changes what the data says (fields, labels, filters, highlights, results)
- Changes: Fields and labels (`field-overlays`), Active field (`active-field`), Filters (`filters`), Colors (`colors`), Highlights (`highlights`), Views (`views`)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `field` | object (`source`, `key`) | yes | A categorical column of the cells by name (source "obs"). |
| `category` | string | yes | A category label as the legend shows it. Not empty. |
| `unassigned_label` | string | no | The category the cells move into, made when missing. Not empty. Default `"unassigned"`. |

Example:

```json
{"field":{"source":"obs","key":"cell_type"},"category":"T cells"}
```

Timeline label: Deleted the category T cells of cell_type

Pseudocode: `delete_category("cell_type", "T cells")`


Pseudocode: `merge_categories("cell_type", "T cells", into="T cells")`

|---|---|---|---|

### `field.consensus`

**Build the consensus column.** The community annotation's consensus for a categorical column as a column of its own: each cell gets the agreed label of its category, or the status of a category without one (disputed, pending); built again under the same name, it is replaced. The outcome of each category is named in the parameters, so it replays by name on any dataset with the same column and categories.

- Agent tool: `field_consensus`
- Effect: `state`: it changes what the data says (fields, labels, filters, highlights, results)
- Changes: Fields and labels (`field-overlays`), Active field (`active-field`), Filters (`filters`), Colors (`colors`)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `key` | string | yes | The consensus column's name. Not empty. |
| `field` | object (`source`, `key`) | yes | The annotated column the consensus is of. |
| `mapping` | list of object (`category`, `status`, `label`, `voters`) | yes | The outcome of each category of the column (a category left out is pending). At least 1 item. |
| `settings` | object (`minAnnotators`, `threshold`) | yes | The consensus rule it was built with. |
| `provenance` | object (`repository`, `branch`, `commit`, `pulledAt`) | yes | Where the votes came from. |

Example:

```json
{"key":"x","field":{"source":"obs","key":"cell_type"},"mapping":[{"category":"T cells","status":"consensus","label":"x","voters":0}],"settings":{"minAnnotators":0,"threshold":-1},"provenance":{"repository":"x","branch":"x","commit":"x","pulledAt":"x"}}
```

Timeline label: Built the consensus column x of cell_type

Pseudocode: `consensus_column("x", of="cell_type", mapping={"T cells": "x"})`

### `field.create-from-pages`

**Make a field from highlight pages.** A new categorical column whose categories are highlight pages: each page's cells take its label; cells on several pages follow the overlap rule.

- Agent tool: `field_create_from_pages`
- Effect: `state`: it changes what the data says (fields, labels, filters, highlights, results)
- Changes: Fields and labels (`field-overlays`)
- Depends on: Highlights (`highlights`), Open cells (`cells`)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `key` | string | yes | The new column's name. Not empty. |
| `pages` | list of object (`page`, `label`) | yes | The pages, in order (first and last refer to it), each with its category label. At least 1 item. |
| `uncovered_label` | string | no | The category of cells on no page; empty leaves them without one. Default `"Unassigned"`. |
| `overlap` | one of `"first"`, `"last"`, `"overlap-label"`, `"intersections"` | no | Cells on several pages: the first page's label, the last's, the overlap label, or one label per combination of pages. Default `"first"`. |
| `overlap_label` | string | no | The label of cells on several pages when overlap is "overlap-label". Default `"Overlap"`. |
| `intersection_labels` | list of object (`pages`, `label`) | no | With overlap "intersections": the label of each combination of pages that has cells. Default `[]`. |

Example:

```json
{"key":"x","pages":[{"page":"x","label":"T cells"}]}
```

Timeline label: Made x from 1 highlight page

Pseudocode: `field_from_pages("x", {"x": "T cells"})`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |

| `field` | object (`source`, `key`) | yes | A categorical column of the cells by name (source "obs"). |
| `visible` | boolean | yes |  |


### `filter.category.cell-count`

**Keep N cells of a category.** Show only `count` cells of one category, a random sample drawn with `seed` (the same seed and count show the same cells; a larger count adds cells); null shows all its cells again.

- Effect: `state`: it changes what the data says (fields, labels, filters, highlights, results)
- Changes: Filters (`filters`)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `field` | object (`source`, `key`) | yes | A categorical column of the cells by name (source "obs"). |
| `category` | string | yes | A category label as the legend shows it. Not empty. |
| `count` | integer or null | yes | How many of its cells stay shown; null for all of them. At least 0. |
| `seed` | integer | no | The sample's seed. At least 0, at most 4294967295. Default `0`. |

Example:

```json
{"field":{"source":"obs","key":"cell_type"},"category":"T cells","count":0}
```

## Data

### `cells.open`

**Open a share of the cells.** Read the dataset again with every cell, or with exactly `count` cells chosen by a subsample method; highlights, labels, views and filters are kept for the cells still open.

- Agent tool: `cells_open`
- Effect: `state`: it changes what the data says (fields, labels, filters, highlights, results)
- Changes: Open cells (`cells`), Data mapping (`mapping`), Fields and labels (`field-overlays`), Gene sets (`gene-sets`), Views (`views`), Active field (`active-field`), Filters (`filters`), Colors (`colors`), Hidden cells (`visibility`), Highlights (`highlights`), Camera (`camera`), Settings (`settings`), Analysis (`analysis`)
- A newer one replaces one still running

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | one of `"all"`, `"subsample"` | yes |  |
| `count` | integer | no | Subsample: how many cells. At least 1. |
| `method` | one of `"uniform"`, `"blocks"`, `"stratified"`, `"spatial"`, `null` | no | Subsample: how the cells are chosen; null for the file's default. Default `null`. |
| `seed` | integer or null | no | Subsample: its seed; null for the file's. At least 0, at most 4294967295. Default `null`. |
| `field` | string | no | Stratified: the categorical column it is stratified by. Not empty. |
| `allocation` | one of `"proportional"`, `"balanced"` | no | Stratified: how the cells are split over the categories. Default `"proportional"`. |
| `embedding` | string | no | Spatial: the obsm embedding it thins. Not empty. |

Example:

```json
{"mode":"all"}
```

Timeline label: Opened every cell

Pseudocode: `open_cells("all")`

### `cells.read-genes`

**Read genes for more cells.** Read every gene for the first `cells` open cells (a dataset stored cell by cell reads genes for a sample of the open cells); stopping keeps what was read.

- Agent tool: `cells_read_genes`
- Effect: `state`: it changes what the data says (fields, labels, filters, highlights, results)
- Changes: Open cells (`cells`)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cells` | integer | yes | How many of the open cells; more than are open reads every one. At least 1. |

Example:

```json
{"cells":1}
```

Timeline label: Read genes for 1 cell

Pseudocode: `read_genes_for(1)`

### `mapping.set`

**Change the data mapping.** Choose which stored arrays are the embeddings, neighbour graph, genes (modality, expression matrix, gene names, log1p, highly variable), latent space and vector fields; groups not named stay as they are. Applied as one change: refused, nothing changes.

- Agent tool: `mapping_set`
- Effect: `state`: it changes what the data says (fields, labels, filters, highlights, results)
- Changes: Data mapping (`mapping`), Views (`views`), Active field (`active-field`), Filters (`filters`), Colors (`colors`), Camera (`camera`), Analysis (`analysis`)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `embeddings` | object (`enabled`, `defaults`) | no | The embeddings views can show, sorted by key then columns, and the default of each dimension. |
| `knn` | string or null | no | The obsp neighbour graph, or null for none. Not empty. |
| `modality` | string | no | The modality genes are read from (a dataset of several). Not empty. |
| `gene_names` | string | no | "index", or "column:&lt;var column>". Not empty. |
| `expression` | string or null | no | "X", "raw", "layer:&lt;name>", or null for no genes. Not empty. |
| `log1p` | list of object (`matrix`, `base`) | no | Each expression matrix that holds log1p values, with its base (null: e). |
| `highly_variable` | string or null | no | The boolean var column marking highly variable genes, or null. Not empty. |
| `latent` | string or null | no | The obsm latent space outlier filters use, or null. Not empty. |
| `vector_fields` | list of object (`key`, `embedding`) | no | Vector fields bound to enabled embeddings, sorted by embedding then key. |

Example:

```json
{}
```

Timeline label: Applied the data mapping

Pseudocode: `set_data_mapping()`

## Highlights

### `highlight.category`

**Highlight a category.** Add the cells of one category of a field, as the selected view shows them, as a group.

- Agent tool: `highlight_category`
- Effect: `state`: it changes what the data says (fields, labels, filters, highlights, results)
- Changes: Highlights (`highlights`)
- Depends on: Open cells (`cells`), Data mapping (`mapping`), Fields and labels (`field-overlays`), Filters (`filters`), Hidden cells (`visibility`), Views (`views`)
- Run again on a stale step (the State panel) brings its result up to date

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `field` | object (`source`, `key`) | yes | A categorical field, by name. |
| `category` | string or number or boolean | yes | The category, by its label as the legend shows it. |
| `page` | string | no | The page the group goes on, by name; a page of that name is made when there is none. Omitted: the page shown, or with `color`, a page of that colour. Not empty. |
| `color` | string | no | The colour of the page the group goes on. With `page`, the colour of the page made (an existing page must already have it). Without, the page shown when it has this colour, else the first page that has it, else a new page of it. |

Example:

```json
{"field":{"source":"obs","key":"cell_type"},"category":"T cells"}
```

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `view` | string | yes | A view: "View N" as the Compare views list numbers its rows (the live view is View 1 while it is shown, the kept views follow in the order they were kept). |


## Camera path

### `camera-path.clear`

**Clear the camera path.** Delete every keyframe of the camera path; playback stops where the camera is.

- Agent tool: `camera_path_clear`
- Effect: `view`: it changes how the data is shown
- Changes: Camera path (`camera-path`)

It takes no parameters.

Example:

```json
{}
```

Timeline label: Cleared the camera path

Pseudocode: `clear_camera_path()`

### `camera-path.duration.set`

**Set a camera path transition time.** Set how long the camera takes from one keyframe to the next, or from every keyframe to its next.

- Agent tool: `camera_path_duration_set`
- Effect: `view`: it changes how the data is shown
- Changes: Camera path (`camera-path`)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `keyframe` | string | no | The keyframe the transition starts at; omitted, every keyframe. Not empty. |
| `seconds` | number or null | yes | Seconds of the transition to the next keyframe, at least 0.1; null paces it automatically. At least 0.1. |

Example:

```json
{"seconds":0.1}
```

Timeline label: Set every camera path transition to 0.1 s

Pseudocode: `set_keyframe_duration(None, 0.1)`

### `camera-path.keyframe.add`

**Add a camera path keyframe.** Save a camera as the next keyframe of the camera path (before the return to start, when there is one).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|

| `label` | string | no | The keyframe's label; omitted, "KF n". Unique among the keyframes. Not empty. |
| `embedding` | object (`key`, `columns`) or null | no | The embedding the keyframe was recorded on; omitted, the one the selected view shows. |

Example:

```json
{}
```

Timeline label: Saved camera path keyframe "new"

Pseudocode: `add_keyframe()`

### `camera-path.keyframe.move`

**Move a camera path keyframe.** Move a keyframe one place earlier (up) or later (down) in the camera path.

|---|---|---|---|
| `keyframe` | string | yes | A keyframe, by its label as the Camera path list shows it. Not empty. |
| `direction` | one of `"up"`, `"down"` | yes | "up" one place earlier, "down" one place later. |

Example:


- Effect: `view`: it changes how the data is shown

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `keyframe` | string | yes | A keyframe, by its label as the Camera path list shows it. Not empty. |


### `camera-path.keyframe.rename`

**Rename a camera path keyframe.** Give a keyframe another label, unique among the keyframes.

- Agent tool: `camera_path_keyframe_rename`
- Effect: `view`: it changes how the data is shown
- Changes: Camera path (`camera-path`)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|


Timeline label: Renamed camera path keyframe "x" to "x"

### `camera-path.loop-back.set`

**End the camera path at its start.** Add or remove a last keyframe that returns the camera to the first one (two keyframes or more).

- Agent tool: `camera_path_loop_back_set`
- Effect: `view`: it changes how the data is shown
- Changes: Camera path (`camera-path`)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | yes | true to end with the return, false to remove it. |

Example:

```json
{"enabled":false}
```

Timeline label: Removed the camera path's return to its start

Pseudocode: `set_keyframe_loop_back(False)`

### `camera-path.playback.set`

**Set camera path playback.** Set how the camera path plays: interpolation, easing, speed of automatic transitions, loop and autoplay.

- Agent tool: `camera_path_playback_set`
- Effect: `view`: it changes how the data is shown
- Changes: Camera path (`camera-path`)
- Repeated at once (a drag, a gesture), it is one step

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `position_interpolation` | one of `"catmull-rom"`, `"linear"`, `"bezier"` | no | How positions between keyframes are drawn. |
| `rotation_interpolation` | one of `"slerp"`, `"linear"` | no | How the view direction turns between keyframes. |
| `easing` | one of `"linear"`, `"ease-in-out"`, `"ease-in"`, `"ease-out"` | no | How each transition speeds up and slows down. |
| `speed` | integer | no | Speed of automatic transitions, 1 (very slow) to 100 (very fast). At least 1, at most 100. |
| `loop` | boolean | no | Play the path again from its start when it ends. |
| `autoplay` | boolean | no | Start playing as soon as the path has two keyframes. |

Example:

```json
{}
```

Timeline label: Set camera path playback: unchanged

Pseudocode: `set_camera_path_playback()`

## Settings

### `figure-export.set`

**Change figure export settings.** Set Figure export options: size, frame, background, fonts, title and axis labels, axes, legend, preview, what Export downloads; only those given change, nothing is exported.

- Agent tool: `figure_export_set`
- Effect: `view`: it changes how the data is shown
- Changes: Settings (`settings`)
- Repeated at once (a drag, a gesture), it is one step

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `size_preset` | one of `"screen-half"`, `"screen"`, `"1200x900"`, `"1600x1200"`, `"1920x1080"` | no | The size preset shown in the panel. |
| `width` | integer | no | Plot width in CSS pixels. At least 100, at most 20000. |
| `height` | integer | no | Plot height in CSS pixels. At least 100, at most 20000. |
| `frame` | object (`lock_aspect`, `rect`) or null | no | The part of the view exported (needs the preview on), or null for the whole view. |
| `background` | one of `"viewer"`, `"white"`, `"transparent"`, `"custom"` | no | The background: the viewer's, white, transparent or custom. |
| `background_color` | string | no | The custom background colour, lowercase #rrggbb. |
| `font_family` | one of `"Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif"`, `"Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif"`, `"\"Times New Roman\", Times, serif"` | no | The font of every text. |
| `auto_text_size` | boolean | no | Size the text from the figure's size (font_sizes is then null). |
| `font_sizes` | object (`base`, `legend`, `ticks`, `axis_label`, `title`, `centroid_label`) or null | no | Text sizes in pixels while auto_text_size is off, else null. |
| `title_follows_dataset` | boolean | no | The title is the dataset's name (title is then null). |
| `title` | string or null | no | The figure title while it does not follow the dataset, else null. |
| `x_label` | string | no | The x axis label. |
| `y_label` | string | no | The y axis label. |
| `include_axes` | boolean | no | Draw the axes. |
| `include_legend` | boolean | no | Draw the legend. |
| `reference_grid` | boolean | no | Draw a reference grid. |
| `show_orientation` | boolean | no | Draw the 3D orientation indicator. |
| `depth_sort` | boolean | no | Draw 3D points back to front. |
| `legend_position` | one of `"right"`, `"bottom"` | no | Where the legend goes. |
| `emphasize_selection` | boolean | no | Fade the cells that are not highlighted. |
| `selection_muted_opacity` | number | no | The opacity of the faded cells, 0 to 1. At least 0, at most 1. |
| `preview` | object (`enabled`, `colorblind_mode`) | no | The preview in the panel and the colour-vision deficiency it simulates. |
| `download` | one of `"svg"`, `"png"`, `"svg+png"`, `"png-multi"`, `"all"` | no | What Export downloads. |
| `dpi` | one of `150`, `300`, `600` | no | The resolution of a PNG. |
| `svg_strategy` | one of `"full-vector"`, `"optimized-vector"`, `"hybrid"`, `null` | no | How an SVG draws many points, or null until chosen. |
| `optimized_target_count` | integer | no | How many points an optimized SVG keeps. At least 1000, at most 5000000. |
| `export_all_views` | boolean | no | Export every view of the multiview, side by side. |

Example:

```json
{"width":1200,"height":900,"include_axes":false}
```

Timeline label: Figure export: width 1200, height 900, include axes off

Pseudocode: `set_figure_export(width=1200, height=900, include_axes=false)`

| `citation` | string or null |  |
| `cells` | object (`total`, `open`, `share`, `subsample`, `digest`) |  |
| `genes` | object (`count`, `read_for`) |  |
| `embeddings` | list of object (`name`, `dimension`) |  |
| `fields` | object (`categorical`, `continuous`, `user_defined`) |  |

### `field.categories`

**Read the categories of a field.** Each category of a categorical field with its cells, the cells shown in the active view, its colour and whether it is shown.

- Agent tool: `field_categories`
- Effect: `read`: it reads, changes nothing and records no step

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `field` | object (`source`, `key`) | yes | A field by name: source "obs" for a column of the cells, "var" for a gene; key is the name as shown. |

Example:

```json
{"field":{"source":"obs","key":"cell_type"}}
```

It returns:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `field` | string |  |
| `view` | string | The view the colours and shown counts are of (the selected one), named as actions name views ("View N"). |
| `categories` | list of object (`label`, `cells`, `visible`, `color`, `shown`) |  |
| `missing` | integer | Open cells without a category. At least 0. |

### `field.summary`

**Summarise a field per category.** A continuous field or a gene per category of a categorical field (cells, mean, median, range, share above zero), or a categorical field's top categories per category.

- Agent tool: `field_summary`
- Effect: `read`: it reads, changes nothing and records no step

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `field` | object (`source`, `key`) | yes | A field by name: source "obs" for a column of the cells, "var" for a gene; key is the name as shown. |
| `by` | object (`source`, `key`) | yes | The categorical obs field to group the cells by. |
| `top` | integer | no | For a categorical field: at most this many of its categories per group. At least 1. Default `50`. |
| `visible_only` | boolean | no | Only the cells the active view shows. Default `false`. |

Example:

```json
{"field":{"source":"obs","key":"cell_type"},"by":{"source":"obs","key":"cell_type"}}
```

It returns:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `field` | object (`source`, `key`, `kind`) |  |
| `by` | string |  |
| `read_for` | object (`cells`, `of`) or null | For a gene read for a sample of the open cells: the cells its statistics are of. |
| `groups` | list of object (`label`, `cells`, `mean`, `median`, `min`, `max`, `above_zero`, `top`) |  |

### `fields.list`

**List the fields.** The cell annotations (obs fields) with their kind and, for a categorical one, how many categories it has.

- Agent tool: `fields_list`
- Effect: `read`: it reads, changes nothing and records no step

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | one of `"categorical"`, `"continuous"` | no | Only fields of this kind. |
| `query` | string | no | Only fields whose key contains this text (any case). Not empty. |

Example:

```json
{}
```

It returns:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `fields` | list of object (`key`, `kind`, `categories`, `user_defined`) |  |

### `genes.search`

**Search the genes.** Gene names matching what is typed, best first, as the gene search box ranks them.

- Agent tool: `genes_search`
- Effect: `read`: it reads, changes nothing and records no step

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `query` | string | yes | Not empty. |
| `limit` | integer | no | At most this many names. At least 1. Default `20`. |

Example:

```json
{"query":"CD3"}
```

It returns:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `genes` | list of string |  |
| `matches` | integer | How many genes match in all. At least 0. |
| `total` | integer | How many genes the dataset has. At least 0. |

| Field | Type | Notes |

| `analysis` | one of `"markers"`, `"differential"`, `"dotplot"`, `"signature"`, `"composition"`, `"quick"`, `"detailed"`, `"correlation"` | yes | The analysis: markers (marker genes), differential (differential expression), dotplot, signature (gene signature), composition, quick, detailed, correlation. |
| `expanded` | object (`width`, `height`, `optionsWidth`, `footerHeight`, `statsWidth`) | yes | The expanded view's box and its splits, in CSS pixels. |

Example:

```json
{"analysis":"markers","expanded":{"width":900,"height":600,"optionsWidth":260,"footerHeight":180,"statsWidth":320}}
```

Timeline label: Resized the expanded view of Marker genes

Pseudocode: `size_analysis_view("markers", width=900, height=600)`

### `analysis.view.set`

**Change how an analysis is shown.** Open or close its option groups, and choose what its result shows (marker genes: list or heatmap, the group listed, the heatmap's look; gene signature: the set shown; the options of the plot its expanded view draws); nothing runs.

- Agent tool: `analysis_view_set`
- Effect: `view`: it changes how the data is shown
- Changes: Analysis (`analysis`)
- Repeated at once (a drag, a gesture), it is one step

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `analysis` | one of `"markers"`, `"differential"`, `"dotplot"`, `"signature"`, `"composition"`, `"correlation"` | yes | An analysis with an options form. |
| `in` | `"panel"` or integer | no | Default `"panel"`. |
| `view` | object (`more`, `groups`, `show`, `group`, `heatmap`, `set`, `plot`) | yes | What to change of how the analysis is shown (only the keys given). |

Example:

```json
{"analysis":"markers","view":{"show":"list"}}
```

Timeline label: Showed Marker genes as a list

Pseudocode: `analysis_view("markers", {"show":"list"})`

### `analysis.window.close`

**Close an analysis window.** Close a floating analysis window (its settings and result go with it; undo brings it back).

- Effect: `state`: it changes what the data says (fields, labels, filters, highlights, results)
- Changes: Analysis (`analysis`), Layout (`layout`)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `window` | integer | yes | A floating analysis window, by its number (1 is the first open). At least 1. |

```json
{"window":1}
```

Timeline label: Closed analysis window 1

### `analysis.window.collapse`

**Collapse or expand an analysis window.** Fold a floating analysis window to its title bar, or unfold it again; its analysis is kept.

- Effect: `layout`: it changes the panels, sections or theme
- Changes: Layout (`layout`)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `window` | integer | yes | A floating analysis window, by its number (1 is the first open). At least 1. |
| `collapsed` | boolean | yes | True folds it to its title bar, false unfolds it. |

Example:

```json
{"window":1,"collapsed":false}
```

Timeline label: Expanded analysis window 1

Pseudocode: `collapse_analysis_window(1, False)`

### `analysis.window.copy`

**Copy an analysis window.** Open a new floating window with a window's analysis and settings.

- Agent tool: `analysis_window_copy`
- Effect: `state`: it changes what the data says (fields, labels, filters, highlights, results)
- Changes: Analysis (`analysis`), Layout (`layout`)
- Depends on: Open cells (`cells`), Data mapping (`mapping`), Fields and labels (`field-overlays`), Filters (`filters`), Hidden cells (`visibility`), Views (`views`), Highlights (`highlights`)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `window` | integer | yes | A floating analysis window, by its number (1 is the first open). At least 1. |

```json
{"window":1}
```

### `analysis.window.place`

**Move or resize an analysis window.** Give a floating analysis window a place and size; it is kept inside the window.

|---|---|---|---|

## Datasets

### `dataset.open`

**Open a dataset.** Open a dataset by the name the person gives: a built-in sample, one of their datasets (My datasets), a link, or an accession the link box takes. It replaces the open dataset; that one's history stays kept in this browser and the new one starts its own. A whole-file download is asked about first.

- Agent tool: `dataset_open`
- Effect: `dataset`: it opens another dataset, whose history starts anew (the open one's stays kept in this browser), and records no step
- Asks the person first when an agent takes it: it downloads a lot (`large-download`)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | A sample's name or id, a name from My datasets, a link to a dataset (a file, a Zarr store, a dataset folder, a CELLxGENE, Zenodo, Figshare or GitHub address), an accession (GSE123456, a DOI), or a Cellucid server (localhost:8765). Not empty. |
| `kind` | one of `"any"`, `"sample"`, `"my-datasets"`, `"link"` | no | Where to look for the name: any (samples, then My datasets, then as a link), sample, my-datasets or link. Default `"any"`. |

Example:

```json
{"name":"Pancreatic endocrinogenesis (scVelo)"}
```

It returns:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | The dataset now open, as Cellucid names it. |
| `kind` | one of `"sample"`, `"link"`, `"server"`, `"file"`, `"folder"`, `"notebook"` | Where it opens from: a built-in sample, a link, a Cellucid server, a file or folder of the person's computer, or a notebook (Python, R) that serves it. |
| `cells` | integer | The cells open (a share of the dataset when it is subsampled). At least 0. |
| `total_cells` | integer | At least 0. |
| `genes` | integer or null | At least 0. |
| `saved_states` | integer | Histories of this dataset kept in this browser from earlier visits; the person was offered to continue the latest. At least 0. |
| `already_open` | boolean | It was open already, so nothing was opened again and its history goes on. |

Timeline label: Opened Pancreatic endocrinogenesis (scVelo)

Pseudocode: `open_dataset("Pancreatic endocrinogenesis (scVelo)")`

### `dataset.share-link`

**Make a share link.** The public link that opens the dataset shown on www.cellucid.com for anyone, with its "Open in Cellucid" badge and an embed snippet, as Share in Session › Open data makes them; what a link carried to grant access is left out. Refused for a dataset no link reopens (a file of this computer, a notebook's, a server on this computer).

- Agent tool: `dataset_share_link`
- Effect: `outside`: it acts outside the dataset's state and history (writes a file the person receives, publishes, or keeps or removes something in this browser for later visits), which the history cannot take back, and records no step
- Asks the person first when an agent takes it: it publishes (`publishes`)

It takes no parameters.

Example:

```json
{}
```

It returns:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `link` | string | The link. |
| `badge` | string | The badge as Markdown. |
| `embed` | string | The embed snippet as HTML. |
| `access_left_out` | boolean | The dataset's link carried a key, a signature or a token that was left out: someone without access cannot open it. |

Timeline label: Made a share link

Pseudocode: `share_link()`

### `datasets.list`

**List the datasets to open.** The datasets this tab can open by name: the built-in samples and the person's own datasets opened before in this browser (My datasets, each with its size and what this browser keeps of it), with the one open now.

- Agent tool: `datasets_list`
- Effect: `read`: it reads, changes nothing and records no step

It takes no parameters.

Example:

```json
{}
```

It returns:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `open` | object (`name`, `kind`) or null | The dataset open now, or null. |
| `samples` | list of object (`name`, `id`, `cells`, `genes`) |  |
| `my_datasets` | list of object (`name`, `kind`, `cells`, `genes`, `last_opened`, `saved_states`, `size`, `saved_states_bytes`, `kept_bytes`, `agent_can_open`) | Most recently opened first. |

### `my-datasets.forget`

**Forget a dataset of My datasets.** Remove one dataset from My datasets, as its Forget in My datasets › All… does: the entry and, for a file or folder of this computer, the browser's handle of it; its saved states only when asked. The dataset itself is not touched, and nothing brings the entry back but opening it again.

- Agent tool: `my_datasets_forget`
- Effect: `outside`: it acts outside the dataset's state and history (writes a file the person receives, publishes, or keeps or removes something in this browser for later visits), which the history cannot take back, and records no step
- Asks the person first when an agent takes it: it deletes something saved (`deletes-saved`)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | Its name in My datasets (datasets_list). Not empty. |
| `saved_states` | boolean | no | Also delete its saved states (histories kept in this browser). Default `false`. |

Example:

```json
{"name":"Pancreatic endocrinogenesis (scVelo)"}
```

It returns:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | The dataset forgotten. |
| `handles` | integer | Handles of files of this computer forgotten with it. At least 0. |
| `saved_states` | integer | Its saved states deleted. At least 0. |

Timeline label: Forgot Pancreatic endocrinogenesis (scVelo) in My datasets

Pseudocode: `forget_dataset("Pancreatic endocrinogenesis (scVelo)")`

## Stored

### `stored.list`

**List what this browser keeps.** Everything kept in this browser for later visits, as the Stored dialog lists it: per dataset (its file's name and host) the converted copies, downloads, downloaded parts and gene indexes with their sizes; then the saved states, My datasets, the connection speeds and the decoder choices; and how much room the browser gives the site.

- Agent tool: `stored_list`
- Effect: `read`: it reads, changes nothing and records no step

It takes no parameters.

Example:

```json
{}
```

It returns:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `datasets` | list of object (`name`, `host`, `bytes`, `items`) | Most recently used first. |
| `saved_states` | object (`count`, `bytes`) | The histories kept in this browser (history_saved_list lists each). |
| `my_datasets` | object (`count`, `files`) | The datasets opened in this browser (datasets_list lists each) and the files of this computer among them it can reopen. |
| `connection_speeds` | integer | Hosts whose connection speed is remembered. At least 0. |
| `decoder_choices` | integer | Decoder choices measured in this browser. At least 0. |
| `bytes` | integer | What the kept items and saved states take. At least 0. |
| `room` | object (`usage`, `quota`, `kept_when_space_is_low`) | What the browser says of the site's storage. |

### `stored.remove`

**Remove what this browser keeps.** Remove what the Stored dialog removes: kept items by id, all a dataset's kept items, every saved state, My datasets (the list and the files' handles), the connection speeds, the decoder choices, or everything (Remove all). An item an open tab uses stays until that tab closes. Nothing brings it back; the dataset opens again more slowly the first time.

- Agent tool: `stored_remove`
- Effect: `outside`: it acts outside the dataset's state and history (writes a file the person receives, publishes, or keeps or removes something in this browser for later visits), which the history cannot take back, and records no step
- Asks the person first when an agent takes it: it deletes something saved (`deletes-saved`)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `items` | list of string | no | Kept items by id (stored_list). At least 1 item, each once. |
| `dataset` | string | no | Every kept item of the dataset with this file name (stored_list). Not empty. |
| `saved_states` | boolean | no | Every saved state of this browser (history_saved_delete deletes one). Default `false`. |
| `my_datasets` | boolean | no | My datasets: the list and the handles of its files (my_datasets_forget forgets one). Default `false`. |
| `connection_speeds` | boolean | no | The connection speeds remembered per host. Default `false`. |
| `decoder_choices` | boolean | no | The decoder choices measured in this browser. Default `false`. |
| `everything` | boolean | no | Everything no open tab uses, as Remove all. Default `false`. |

Example:

```json
{}
```

It returns:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `removed` | integer | Kept items removed. At least 0. |
| `held` | integer | Kept items that stay, in use by an open tab. At least 0. |
| `saved_states` | integer | Saved states deleted. At least 0. |
| `my_datasets` | integer | Datasets forgotten from My datasets. At least 0. |
| `connection_speeds` | integer | Hosts whose connection speed was forgotten. At least 0. |
| `decoder_choices` | integer | Decoder choices forgotten. At least 0. |
| `said` | string | What the dialog says of it. |

Timeline label: Removed what this browser keeps

Pseudocode: `stored_remove()`

## Exports

### `cells.export`

**Export the highlighted cells.** Write the highlighted cells of a highlight page as a file, as the Highlights list's export buttons do: an obs-column CSV (every open cell, a true/false column per highlight, which cellucid.pull() in Python and cellucid_pull() in R read back) or an .h5ad subset of the highlighted cells with their expression rows. The .h5ad reads the cells' expression first; its time and bytes are estimated from this connection before it starts.

- Agent tool: `cells_export`
- Effect: `outside`: it acts outside the dataset's state and history (writes a file the person receives, publishes, or keeps or removes something in this browser for later visits), which the history cannot take back, and records no step
- Asks the person first when an agent takes it: it writes a file (`writes-file`)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `page` | string | no | The highlight page; the page shown when left out. Not empty. |
| `format` | one of `"csv"`, `"h5ad"` | no | csv: the obs-column CSV; h5ad: an AnnData file of the highlighted cells. Default `"csv"`. |

Example:

```json
{}
```

It returns:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `file` | string | The file written. |
| `bytes` | integer | At least 0. |
| `format` | one of `"csv"`, `"h5ad"` |  |
| `page` | string | The highlight page exported. |
| `cells` | integer | Cells highlighted on it. At least 0. |
| `renamed` | list of object (`key`, `name`) | Names an .h5ad cannot hold as they are, written under other names. |

Timeline label: Exported the highlighted cells as CSV

Pseudocode: `export_cells()`

### `field.export`

**Export a field.** Write a column of the cells (categorical or continuous) as an obs-column CSV, as its Export button in Color by does: every open cell and its value, which cellucid.pull() in Python and cellucid_pull() in R read back.

- Agent tool: `field_export`
- Effect: `outside`: it acts outside the dataset's state and history (writes a file the person receives, publishes, or keeps or removes something in this browser for later visits), which the history cannot take back, and records no step
- Asks the person first when an agent takes it: it writes a file (`writes-file`)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `field` | object (`source`, `key`) | yes | A column of the cells by name (source "obs"), categorical or continuous. |

Example:

```json
{"field":{"source":"obs","key":"cell_type"}}
```

It returns:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `file` | string | The file written. |
| `bytes` | integer | At least 0. |
| `field` | string | The field exported. |
| `kind` | one of `"categorical"`, `"continuous"` |  |

Timeline label: Exported cell_type as CSV

Pseudocode: `export_field("cell_type")`

### `figure.export`

**Export the figure.** Write the figure of the view shown (every view in a grid when the settings say so) as its Download button does, with the figure export's settings as they are (figure_export_set changes them: format, size, labels, legend, style): one SVG or PNG file, or several in one ZIP archive. Refused, saying why, when the figure cannot reproduce what the view shows (a render mode other than points, an overlay it cannot draw).

- Agent tool: `figure_export`
- Effect: `outside`: it acts outside the dataset's state and history (writes a file the person receives, publishes, or keeps or removes something in this browser for later visits), which the history cannot take back, and records no step
- Asks the person first when an agent takes it: it writes a file (`writes-file`)

It takes no parameters.

Example:

```json
{}
```

It returns:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `files` | list of object (`format`, `file`, `dpi`) | The figures written: one file, or several in one ZIP archive. |
| `zip` | boolean | The files were written in one ZIP archive (several formats or resolutions). |

Timeline label: Exported the figure

Pseudocode: `export_figure()`

## Community annotation

### `annotation.suggest`

**Suggest a label.** Suggest a label for a category in the person's name, with their upvote, as the voting dialog's New suggestion does, and publish that suggestion alone: the person's own file in the community annotation repository is written as published now plus this suggestion (a pull request when they cannot write to the repository), which others see on their next Pull. A label already suggested for the category is refused with its id (vote on it instead). Asked of the person first; the history cannot take it back. Refused until the person has connected the repository and signed in to GitHub.

- Agent tool: `annotation_suggest`
- Effect: `outside`: it acts outside the dataset's state and history (writes a file the person receives, publishes, or keeps or removes something in this browser for later visits), which the history cannot take back, and records no step
- Asks the person first when an agent takes it: it publishes (`publishes`)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `field` | object (`source`, `key`) | yes | A categorical column of the cells by name (source "obs"). |
| `category` | string | yes | A category label as the legend shows it. Not empty. |
| `label` | string | yes | The label suggested. Not empty. |
| `ontology_id` | string | no | Its ontology term, when known. Not empty. |
| `evidence` | string | no | Why: the markers or reasoning behind it. Not empty. |

Example:

```json
{"field":{"source":"obs","key":"cell_type"},"category":"T cells","label":"CD4+ T cell"}
```

It returns:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `repository` | string | The GitHub repository of the community annotation. |
| `published` | one of `"repository"`, `"pull-request"` | Where the suggestion went: written to the repository, or in a pull request its authors merge. |
| `pull_request` | string or null | The pull request, when it went to one. |
| `id` | string | The suggestion's id (annotation_vote takes it). |
| `label` | string | The label suggested. |
| `not_published` | integer or null | The person's other changes still not published (null when not known). At least 0. |

Timeline label: Suggested "CD4+ T cell" for T cells of cell_type

Pseudocode: `annotation_suggest("cell_type", "T cells", "CD4+ T cell")`

### `annotation.suggestions`

**Read the community annotation.** The labels suggested for the categories of a field by the community annotation of the dataset shown (its connected GitHub repository), with their votes, the person's own vote and each category's consensus, as the voting dialog and the legend show them; whether the field is open for voting, and when this browser last pulled. One page holds what fits a tool result; `next` starts the following one.

- Agent tool: `annotation_suggestions`
- Effect: `read`: it reads, changes nothing and records no step

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `field` | object (`source`, `key`) | yes | A categorical column of the cells by name (source "obs"). |
| `category` | string | no | One category; every category of the field when left out. Not empty. |
| `cursor` | integer | no | Where the page starts: the next of the last page; the first page when left out. At least 0. |

Example:

```json
{"field":{"source":"obs","key":"cell_type"}}
```

It returns:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `repository` | string | The GitHub repository it is kept in. |
| `pulled_at` | string or null | When this browser last pulled from it (an ISO instant), null before the first Pull: votes made since are not here. |
| `annotated` | boolean | The field is open to community annotation. |
| `closed` | boolean | Voting on the field is closed (only its authors still vote). |
| `repository_field` | string | The field's name in the repository, when the person renamed it here. |
| `categories` | list of object (`category`, `repository_category`, `consensus`, `suggestions`) |  |
| `total_categories` | integer | Categories on every page. At least 0. |
| `next` | integer or null | The cursor of the next page; null on the last. At least 0. |

### `annotation.vote`

**Vote on a suggested label.** Vote a suggested label of a category up or down (none takes the person's vote back) and publish that vote alone: the person's own file in the community annotation repository is written as published now plus this vote (a pull request when they cannot write to the repository), which others see on their next Pull. Nothing else of the person's is published, and a vote that changes nothing publishes nothing. Asked of the person first; the history cannot take it back. Refused until the person has connected the repository and signed in to GitHub.

- Agent tool: `annotation_vote`
- Effect: `outside`: it acts outside the dataset's state and history (writes a file the person receives, publishes, or keeps or removes something in this browser for later visits), which the history cannot take back, and records no step
- Asks the person first when an agent takes it: it publishes (`publishes`)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `field` | object (`source`, `key`) | yes | A categorical column of the cells by name (source "obs"). |
| `category` | string | yes | A category label as the legend shows it. Not empty. |
| `suggestion` | string | yes | The suggestion, by its id or its label (annotation_suggestions); suggestions with the same label are one suggestion. Not empty. |
| `vote` | one of `"up"`, `"down"`, `"none"` | yes | up, down, or none to take the person's vote back. |

Example:

```json
{"field":{"source":"obs","key":"cell_type"},"category":"T cells","suggestion":"CD4+ T cell","vote":"up"}
```

It returns:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `repository` | string | The GitHub repository of the community annotation. |
| `published` | one of `"repository"`, `"pull-request"`, `"unchanged"` | Where the vote went: written to the repository, in a pull request its authors merge, or nowhere (it was already so). |
| `pull_request` | string or null | The pull request, when it went to one. |
| `suggestion` | string | The label voted on. |
| `vote` | one of `"up"`, `"down"`, `"none"` | The person's vote on it now. |
| `up` | integer | Its upvotes now. At least 0. |
| `down` | integer | Its downvotes now. At least 0. |
| `not_published` | integer or null | The person's other changes still not published (null when not known). At least 0. |

Timeline label: Voted "CD4+ T cell" up for T cells of cell_type

Pseudocode: `annotation_vote("cell_type", "T cells", "CD4+ T cell", "up")`
